article_title: PostgreSQL November Updates Ask for Some Reindexing and New Full Backups for Incremental-Backup Users; Announcement Calls 14.25 the Final 14 Release

content_preview.title: PostgreSQL November Updates Ask for Some Reindexing and New Full Backups for Incremental-Backup Users; Announcement Calls 14.25 the Final 14 Release
content_preview.summary: The PostgreSQL project's November 12 announcement lists six post-update steps, calls 14.25 the final 14 release and plans PostgreSQL 19 general availability for November 19; the five release-notes pages differ by branch.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25, plus the second release candidate of PostgreSQL 19, in an [announcement posted November 12, 2026](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-187-1712-1616-1520-1425-and-19-rc-2-released-3442/). The project says the update releases fix 52 security vulnerabilities and over 140 bugs, and that there are "several issues that may require you to take extra steps after updating." This arti...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (1,017 words, News range 400-1200; title 148 characters). It separates what the announcement lists (six post-update steps), what the release notes add (extension rebuild, incremental-backup detail, join-removal back-patch), a per-branch comparison, the PostgreSQL 14 end-of-life wording and the PostgreSQL 19 RC 2 schedule. It leaves the 52-CVE list to the announcement and makes no CVE-level claims of its own.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all eight stored snapshots (source-0 to source-7 .html.gz, all HTTP 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for every source). Live curl with a browser User-Agent on 2026-11-13 returned HTTP 200; the announcement (source-0) and the 14.25 notes (source-5) hashed identically to the stored sha256 prefixes (a9b4dab483dcf025, 6ffc69300569144b); the Help Net Security page is dynamic (hash differs) but the live text contains the same 'final release of PostgreSQL 14' sentence. source-0 postgresql.org announcement (Posted on 2026-11-12): confirms 18.7/17.12/16.16/15.20/14.25 plus 19 RC 2, '52 security vulnerabilities and over 140 bugs' (52 CVE lines counted), the 'several issues that may require you to take extra steps' sentence, 'This is the final release of PostgreSQL 14. PostgreSQL 14 is now end-of-life...', the Updating section with exactly six conditional steps (GIN reindex if suspected; pg_trgm gist_trgm_ops reindex; missing chunk number REINDEX TABLE; incremental backups new full backup; partitioned tables NOT NULL NO INHERIT query/repair; bpchar B-tree reindex, 'Columns declared as char(n) are not affected'), no dump/reload needed, skipped-releases sentence, RC 2 note with 19 November 2026 planned GA 'Unless an issue is discovered that requires a delay or an additional release candidate', the Changes Since 19 RC 1 list introduced by 'These include:' (JSON_ARRAY/JSON_OBJECT revert, GROUPING SETS, LISTEN/NOTIFY etc., pg_upgrade/Migration to Version 19 reindex note), the 'significant change for an update release' join-removal sentence, and 'The issues listed below affect PostgreSQL 18. Many of these issues also affect other supported versions'. The announcement text contains no mention of rebuilding extensions (grep for rebuil/C-language/extension finds only CVE titles and the REINDEX CONCURRENTLY sentence), so the article's 'silence, not contradiction' framing is accurate. source-1 18.7 notes (release date 2026-11-12): verbatim 'For full protection, this change requires rebuilding C-language extensions, and there are some extensions that will require source-code changes' plus the composite_type_mismatch parameter sentence ('doing so carries security risks'); 'existing incremental backup files should not be trusted'; 'when both data checksums and wal_log_hints are disabled'; 'This fix does not correct existing WAL summaries, therefore incremental backups taken after updating can still be affected'; join removal 'a significant change that normally we'd never consider back-patching'. source-2 17.12: incremental-backup guidance and fixes (10 mentions), join removal (2), extension-rebuild sentence verbatim (1), no NO INHERIT entry. source-3 16.16: 0 incremental-backup mentions, join removal present, extension sentence verbatim. source-4 15.20: 0 incremental backup, 0 join removal, extension sentence verbatim. source-5 14.25: 0 incremental backup, 0 join removal, extension sentence verbatim, 'This is expected to be the last PostgreSQL release in the 14.X series' (the announcement says 'final', the notes say 'expected to be the last'). I recounted the branch comparison from the raw pages: incremental backup 18.7/17.12 only; join-removal 18.7/17.12/16.16 only; NO INHERIT 18.7 only; extension-rebuild sentence, bpchar, gist_trgm_ops, GIN and missing-chunk entries on all five. Every figure in the article's bullet list matches. source-6 versioning page: 14 / 14.25 / Supported 'Yes' / first release September 30, 2021 / final release November 12, 2026, as the article reports; none of the pages explains the 'final' versus 'expected to be the last' versus 'Yes' difference, so the article's 'reports each wording as published' is accurate. source-7 Help Net Security (Anamarija Pogorelec, 2026-11-13): covers the release itself, repeats 52 CVEs / 140 bugs, lists the GIN, gist_trgm_ops, bpchar, missing-chunk reindex steps and the incremental-backup full-backup step, says 14.25 is the final release of PostgreSQL 14, reports GA 19 November and the JSON_ARRAY/JSON_OBJECT revert; it does not mention the partitioned-table NO INHERIT check (as the article says). It adds CVE-level characterisation (32 of 52 at CVSS 8.8, client tool fixes) that the article deliberately does not use. Independence: ONE independent outlet (Help Net Security); the other seven sources are first-party postgresql.org pages. The News range requires 3-5 sources, with no independence requirement (that applies to Analysis only); 8 cited sources meet the count, and the dependence on first-party pages is disclosed by the article's own wording (the announcement and release notes are the subject). Help Net Security largely restates the announcement but is a separate newsroom, and the article describes it accurately; Phoronix is not cited. Allowlist: postgresql.org and helpnetsecurity.com are already in config/source_allowlist.txt; no additions. Internal link /article/2026-10/17-postgresql-19-rc-1-moves-general-availability-to-november-19-with-a-second-release-candidate-planned-for-november-12 exists, and that article does set 19 November GA and plans RC 2 for 12 November, as the article says. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the story is the PostgreSQL update releases; Anthropic is not the subject and is not named in the headline, summary or lead. The release notes credit 'the Anthropic OSS program' and 'Claude' on reporter lines of security entries (CVE-2026-116315 and others), but the article reports no credit line (it leaves the CVE list to the announcement), and the announcement and Help Net Security do not mention Anthropic; the policy's third trigger (a credit line reported in a passage of its own) is not met.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline: 'Ask for Some Reindexing' is faithful (GIN indexes if suspected, gist_trgm_ops, TOAST/missing chunk, bpchar B-tree; conditional, 'some' fits); 'New Full Backups for Incremental-Backup Users' matches the announcement sentence 'If you use incremental backups, we recommend taking a new full backup' and the 18.7/17.12 notes (the branch list shows it applies to the pages that mention incremental backups only); 'Announcement Calls 14.25 the Final 14 Release' is faithful to 'This is the final release of PostgreSQL 14' and the article reports the softer 14.25 notes wording and the versioning page 'Yes' in the body, so 'Calls' attributes correctly. Summary: six steps (recounted: six), 14.25 final, GA 19 November, branch differences: all supported. Release date 2026-11-12: announcement 'Posted on 2026-11-12' and every notes page 'Release date: 2026-11-12'; the article makes no time-zone claim. RC 2 and 19 November GA: verified. Claim-accuracy greps (only/none/neither/nor/both/all/any/last) run on the extracted submission: 'Neither the announcement nor Help Net Security' estimates installations / explains GIN detection is bounded to two named sources and holds; 'None of the cited pages explains the difference' holds across all eight; 'on the 18.7 page only' (NO INHERIT) holds; 'all five pages' claims hold. The RC 2 list is correctly marked incomplete ('include', 'among others'). CVE claims limited to the count (52, verified by counting CVE lines) in the lead. All quotes are verbatim.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive; Herald-derived counts and comparisons are labelled as the Herald's own; silence is not presented as contradiction.
editor_notes.originality: No existing coverage of the 18.7/17.12/16.16/15.20/14.25 update in src/content/articles; the PG19 RC 1 article (2026-10/17) is the linked predecessor and covers the earlier announcement. Angle (post-update steps and branch differences) is distinct from the CVE list that another writer owns.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed News coverage of an update release with real operator consequences (reindexing, new full backups, branch-specific differences). Headline, summary and lead verified against the raw announcement and all five release-notes pages; no corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate release coverage for PostgreSQL administrators, a defined developer audience.
